summary: Integration brief — annunimas-human tenant: a private/local human-knowledge interface that scans Obsidian-compatible Markdown vaults, parses metadata and wikilinks, and translates notes into Annunimas memory records (src/lib.rs:1-4, src/lib.rs:37-42, src/lib.rs:106-129). Upstream Annunimas: the source platform from which this tenant was copied and which currently supplies its core memory contracts and Mnemosyne integration through direct path dependencies (docs/migration-notes.md:1-10, Cargo.toml:12-14). Shared autonomous-agent safety boundary: agents must distinguish raw, generated, human, governance, and runtime authority; only canonical material is safe for reliance; unresolved conflicts require review rather than guessing; and agents may not silently promote, overwrite, move, or delete human knowledge (docs/human-knowledge-ingestion-contract.md:21-25, docs/human-knowledge-ingestion-contract.md:49-69, docs/human-knowledge-ingestion-contract.md:96-113, docs/human-knowledge-ingestion-contract.md:145-152). Recommendation: implement the planned tenant-facing memory contract, replace direct Annunimas path dependencies with that boundary, then remove the duplicate upstream workspace member after compatibility verification (docs/migration-notes.md:9-10). Tenant risk: MemoryStore::store serializes each record but discards it, so scans appear successful without durable persistence (src/lib.rs:56-89). Upstream Annunimas risk: the direct path dependencies and retained workspace copy create tight coupling and compatibility-drift risk across the migration seam (Cargo.toml:13-14, docs/migration-notes.md:9-10). Declared clean-tree check passed exactly as specified; no files were modified.
